title: Pilotage 1.1 conformance test vectors
description: Engine-neutral, machine-readable test vectors keyed to the requirements of Parts II and III. Each vector states a setup (precondition, prose, engine-neutral), an action (an abstract Pilotage operation request), and expected assertions. Vectors are specifications of tests: a harness binds them to a concrete Server (via the MCP binding of Part III) or evaluates them against a Client implementation. Polarity: 'good' = accepted / behaves correctly; 'bad' = rejected correctly, as a value, never a crash. Reachability: a vector applies only when its 'requires' capabilities are declared by the Language under test.

vectors.setup: Any conformant Server.

assertions: manifest.languages is non-empty
every Language entry's loop names exist in tools/list
loop membership matches the effective capability map (validate always; execute iff declared; trace iff trace_fetch declared)
guides field equals 'pilotage_get_guide'; catalog field equals 'pilotage_catalog' iff catalog declared
no side effects observable

vectors.setup: A handshake MCP revision (initialize present). Part III 3.2 makes the accelerator a MAY: a Server that does not attach it is skipped, not failed.

assertions: when the initialize result carries _meta['io.github.jafarsa0/pilotage'], that object holds manifest and/or manifest_uri
an inline manifest validates as a Manifest
the inline manifest is consistent with the pilotage_manifest result; where they differ, the tool's result is authoritative (it is newer)

vectors.setup: Any conformant Server, approached with no client-side instructions and no prior knowledge: only the connection and the surfaces MCP always shows.

assertions: on a revision with initialize, whenever the Pilotage tools are exposed to the Client, the instructions field names Pilotage (identifier or the word) and directs the agent to call pilotage_manifest first
the pilotage_manifest tool description identifies it as the starting point, sufficient for an agent reading tools/list alone
the pilotage_get_guide description states the learn stage (guides); the pilotage_catalog description states the lookup stage (catalog) when any Language declares catalog
each declared loop tool description states its stage (validate, execute, or trace) and names its Language(s)
the rules constrain communicated content, never wording

vectors.setup: Language with at least one core guide and the closed-sets guide.

assertions: no guide carries a body member
at least one guide has level 'core'
exactly one guide's topics contains 'closed-sets', with level 'reference'

vectors.setup: A known guide id from the index.

assertions: guide.body is a string in the declared format

vectors.setup: A guide id that does not exist.
Language whose guides capability does NOT declare topic_fetch.
Catalog with at least one entry.

assertions: catalog_version present
every entry carries risk and risk_hints

vectors.setup: Catalog with more entries than the Server's page size (or a small explicit limit).

assertions: response carries next_cursor when more results remain
passing next_cursor back unchanged yields the next page
absence of next_cursor on the final page
the union of pages covers every visible entry exactly once

vectors.setup: An entry id that does not exist.

assertions: catalog_version present as sibling of error

vectors.setup: Language whose catalog capability does NOT declare changed_since.
A baseline token the Server cannot compute a delta from.
No catalog changes between two calls by the same caller.

assertions: both responses carry an identical catalog_version

vectors.setup: Between two list calls, one visible entry's defined field (e.g. description) changes.

assertions: the second catalog_version differs from the first

vectors.setup: A program known to be valid at the current catalog.

assertions: valid is true
no error-severity diagnostics
plan present iff plan declared, validating against Plan
catalog_version present iff catalog declared

vectors.setup: A program referencing a name not in the catalog.

assertions: valid is false
at least one diagnostic whose code is a member of the closed-sets guide's enumeration
diagnostic path uses the declared locator dialect

vectors.setup: A program producing only warning-severity diagnostics.

assertions: valid is true
diagnostics non-empty, all severity 'warning'
plan present iff plan declared

vectors.setup: Observable engine state captured before and after.

assertions: no externally observable state change after any call
no catalog entry was invoked

vectors.setup: A program whose step identifier contains '#' or '/' (structured Languages with author-chosen ids).

assertions: valid is false
a diagnostic reports the reserved-character violation

vectors.requirement: Part II 6.4 rule 2; Part III 4.4 rule 10
vectors.setup: Language WITHOUT context_schema.

assertions: valid is false
a diagnostic with reserved code 'context_binding'
not a request error, not a carrier error

vectors.setup: Language WITH a required context_schema; request omits context.

assertions: valid is false
a diagnostic with reserved code 'context_binding'

vectors.setup: A valid program with known effects; current catalog_version supplied.

assertions: outcome is {ok:true, status:'success', error:null}
trace.level equals the effective level (min of requested and declared)
every trace step appears exactly once in execution order
every invoking trace step names its catalog entry in calls

vectors.setup: An invalid inline program submitted directly to execute, without a prior validate.

assertions: outcome status is 'validation_error'
diagnostics present and non-empty
no side effects occurred
run_id present (a refused Run)

vectors.setup: expected_catalog_version set to a stale token (catalog changed after validation).

assertions: outcome status is 'catalog_drift'
no side effects occurred

vectors.setup: A stale token AND an invalid program in the same request.

assertions: outcome status is 'catalog_drift' (drift check precedes re-validation)

vectors.setup: A promoted program whose referenced entry's load-bearing field changed after promotion.

assertions: outcome status is 'promotion_drift'
no side effects occurred

vectors.setup: Request carrying both an inline program and a program_ref.
Request carrying neither runnable.
A promoted program; input violating the promoted entry's input_schema.

assertions: outcome status is 'validation_error'
a diagnostic with reserved code 'input_binding' whose path points into the input value

vectors.setup: trace_level set to an unrecognized value.

assertions: not a carrier (-32602) error

vectors.setup: Language whose execute capability does NOT declare test_run.
Language with execution 'both'; request omits mode.
Two identical execute requests with the same idempotency_key, same runnable, same input.

assertions: exactly one execution occurred
both responses are identical, including run_id

vectors.setup: A second request reusing the same idempotency_key with different input.
A valid branching program where the taken arm is known.

assertions: the branch appears as its own trace entry with a decision whose took equals the plan's arm.label for the taken arm
plan steps of the untaken arm are absent from the trace
every expected-set member appears (matched on base identifier)

vectors.setup: A valid program whose loop condition is false on entry (zero iterations).

assertions: the loop appears as one trace entry carrying a single 'exit' decision
no loop-body steps appear in the trace
outcome is success

vectors.setup: A valid program whose second step deterministically fails mid-run.

assertions: outcome ok is false with status 'partial' or a documented engine status
trace contains the executed prefix
every unprefixed trace entry maps to the expected set by base identifier

vectors.setup: A previously verified valid program.

assertions: run_id and outcome are returned
no trace member in the response

vectors.setup: A previously verified valid program; Language declares trace_fetch.

assertions: run_id is returned (it identifies the Run in-band even when the record is not stored)
a later trace fetch with this run_id yields the not_found request error (store false forbids retention beyond the response)

vectors.setup: A previously verified valid program; Language declares trace_fetch.

assertions: the request is valid: store and trace_level are independent controls over the same record
run_id and outcome are returned; no trace member in the response (trace_level 'none' suppresses only the inline envelope)
a later trace fetch with this run_id returns the stored envelope at the level the Engine recorded

vectors.setup: A Language whose declared retention value is 'none' (such a Language cannot declare trace_fetch).

assertions: the field is rejected, never silently ignored

vectors.setup: A retained started Run executed at level summary or full, within the retention window.

assertions: the fetched envelope is the stored record of the Run: the same trace that rode the execute response
trace.level equals the level at which the Run was recorded

vectors.setup: A retained Run recorded at trace level 'full'.

assertions: trace.level is 'summary': the returned level is the lower of the requested and recorded levels
the fetch door returns no more than was recorded

vectors.setup: Any retained run_id; the fetch request asks for trace_level 'none'.

assertions: 'none' is an execute-time value: it suppresses the inline envelope and has no meaning when asking for a stored record

vectors.setup: Three run_ids: one nonexistent, one unstored (or refused), one belonging to another caller.

assertions: all three results are byte-identical apart from transport framing: kind, message, content text, and structure do not distinguish the cases

vectors.setup: An entry that exists but is not visible to the requesting caller.

assertions: the result is indistinguishable from the nonexistent-entry result of PIL-LOOKUP-GET-UNKNOWN-B
no diagnostic hint anywhere ever names this entry for this caller

vectors.setup: A valid program whose execution fails for a reason the closed-sets guide covers with no more specific engine-defined status.

assertions: outcome ok is false with status 'error' (the reserved fallback)
outcome.error is a non-null string
not reported as a request error or carrier error

vectors.setup: A fault in the Server's own machinery during pre-execution processing (for example, an injected validator crash in a test build).

assertions: no side effects occurred
not an unhandled transport fault

vectors.setup: A program engineered to exceed a validation resource bound (for example, pathological nesting or expansion depth).

assertions: the request terminates within the bound rather than hanging

vectors.setup: Adapted-tier servers only: an invalid program whose validator message matches no classification rule. Native-tier servers assert instead that 'constraint' is enumerated in the closed-sets guide (membership is required even when unreachable).

assertions: valid is false
the diagnostic code is 'constraint', never a value outside the enumerated set

vectors.setup: tools/call naming a tool that does not exist.
A syntactically invalid JSON request body.
A plan whose max_risk_hints has destructive true; no approval granted.

action.scenario: Model requests execute for the planned program

assertions: the Host does not transmit the execute request
approval is requested outside the Model

vectors.setup: Server returns valid:false, then ok:false outcomes.

action.scenario: Client receives diagnostics and failed outcomes

assertions: no transport-level retry is triggered
the loop continues (revision or drift recovery), not abandoned
an unrecognized ok:false status is treated as 'partial'
an unrecognized request-error kind is treated as 'internal'
